intake.limitation: Distinct source locations can produce the same observed-history distribution after changing unobserved source strength, transport history, initial plume and sensor state. Fixed-nuisance source contrast and accurate concentration prediction therefore do not establish source identifiability. The available wind map has neither a stamped joint trajectory distribution nor established calibration, and the environmental plume is already present when the sensor starts.

bottleneck_statement: For inverse localization from one moving sensor, source location is not identified when two locations admit physically allowed source-strength, transport, pre-observation plume and sensor-history explanations with the same law of the actually observed gas/wind/pose history. The primary instance is the user's transient, adaptively sampled indoor UAV stream. Physical dependency-guided sequential inference already marginalizes wind and concentration fields and accounts implicitly for unknown release rate, but its stated model is single-source steady-state dispersion and its conditional fields do not represent an observed-time history with sensor memory (arxiv:2608.16221v1, III-A and III-C). Rank-based mobile STE explicitly simulates slow MOX dynamics and samples in motion, yet its estimator compares ranks against steady DDPM concentration predictions and requires a positive monotonic relation; history-dependent rank reversals are outside that identifying condition (semanticscholar:fb214b8cbae18ea03c0a852ab3097b570c5ac29f, II-C to II-D). IASA already exposes unknown-strength ambiguity, lag, background absorption and weak distinguishability, conditional on declared inventories and transport (arxiv:2608.00050v1, Eqs. 2-6). The unresolved question for this input regime is which physically warranted restrictions exclude wrong-source alternative histories, and when existing observations can validate those restrictions; neither conditional separation in one assumed operator nor sharper inference within that operator establishes that the inferred location is the physical source.

closest_adjacent.summary_and_residue: DGSE-S uses separate learned wind, concentration and source conditionals, marginalizing intermediate fields with Monte Carlo; source release rate and inlet velocity are explicitly unknown inputs whose effects enter through measurements, so neither physical dependency factorization nor nuisance marginalization is absent prior art. Its stated domain is steady-state single-source dispersion, with diagonal per-cell field conditionals and spatial accumulated measurements, and the read method supplies no time-indexed transport/sensor-state model or criterion excluding source versus admissible history ambiguity in the user's transient stream.

closest_adjacent.summary_and_residue: Rank STE compares EDF ranks of measured and predicted concentrations, uses a steady DDPM, and explicitly models first-order MOX response/recovery in simulation while evaluating sense-in-motion sensing. Its rank validity is conditional on positive monotonic alignment, while the likelihood compares spatial predicted concentrations to observed ranks without propagating the candidate's sensor history; temporal filtering that reverses order is not covered by static monotonic invariance, and the method does not derive physical source identifiability after arbitrary transport and initial-history uncertainty.

closest_adjacent.summary_and_residue: IASA constructs wind-history-conditioned lagged source-temporal-basis fingerprints, projects a predeclared source-independent background space, and diagnoses coefficient/ray distinguishability while retaining nonnegative unknown source strengths; it also explicitly uses open boundaries, an initial-condition baseline and constrained transport refinement. Its estimand is inventory-based attribution under that declared operator and nuisance class, so the diagnostic does not establish actual point-source location when unknown ventilation, initial plume and temporally correlated wind/sensor histories admit alternative explanations outside that class.

closest_adjacent.summary_and_residue: Orthogonal calibration permits flexible discrepancy priors and posterior projection, building on a calibration target defined as the loss-minimizing simulator parameter and an orthogonality restriction relative to simulator sensitivity. Its own formulation distinguishes this target from a physically true parameter when the simulator is biased, so imposing orthogonality cannot be cited as proof that a misspecified gas transport model recovers the actual source location; the domain validity of such restrictions remains a separate obligation.

anchor_fulltext_check.role: Literature comparator, not a procedure selected for faithful reimplementation or simulation in Phase 1
anchor_fulltext_check.sufficiency: The read method explicitly fixes the steady-state scope, unknown-rate treatment, conditional inputs and marginalization. These suffice for the scope residue. No algorithmic faithfulness claim is made. If later phases elect to reproduce DGSE or any other paper, they must first pin the full procedure and unresolved parameters.

what_phase_0_did_not_address: Additive; frontier sites dgse and rank: for a moving sensor with memory, a gas sample is generated by exposure along a history, and distinct location/strength/transport histories can induce the same complete sampled record even though their instantaneous fields or fixed-nuisance responses differ. The retrieved mobile methods do not establish the conditions under which the existing joint history distinguishes those locations when the environmental plume predates sensor startup — stakes: the user's UAV can interpret delayed peaks or persistent residual gas as current spatial evidence, concentrating belief at a wrong source and spending its limited search time there.

Subtractive; frontier sites dgse and rank, shared ancestor steady: whether the steady-field summary assumed by these two indoor source-inference branches is sufficient for source identification when source age, environmental initial concentration and sensor history are not known. This is a question about that branch's inherited assumption, not a claim that every retrieved paper assumes steady state — stakes: apparent gains from a physically structured estimator may depend on an unexamined reduction of the data-generating process, preventing their interpretation as evidence for physical source identification in the user's transient setting.

Additive; frontier sites iasa and plume_joint, with orthogonal calibration as an estimand warning: source separability conditional on a declared transport/background class does not establish that this class excludes wrong-source explanations for physically valid reasons. The needed outcome is a source-location claim whose identifying restrictions have testable implications beyond fitting the same gas response, using only the information actually available online — stakes: inventory diagnostics or calibration constraints can produce a unique, precise model-dependent answer while leaving the physical leak location unestablished, undermining both field decisions and the main scientific claim.

method_lineage.notes: Retrieved nodes are citable; parametric nodes are awareness-only and are not novelty evidence. Parent edges describe formulation ancestry, not a claim of documented citation descent. A shallow gap in the 2-4y and 4-8y bands is preferable to invented intermediate methods; the only 2-4y node here is directly retrieved. Five collateral families were checked: dynamic observability, blind deconvolution, partial identification, nuisance profiling and instruments. No collateral node is a gap site or shared ancestor. The steady-state assumption is shared only by the rank/DGSE branch; it is explicitly not imposed on IASA, the joint-inversion branch or the entire field.

phase2_hard_constraints: Specify the estimand: actual source cell/location versus a simulator-calibration parameter or identified set. Do not silently substitute a loss-minimizing pseudo-true source for the physical source.

Do not claim location identification under unrestricted transport discrepancy, arbitrary unknown initial gas field and arbitrary source history. State the load-bearing restrictions, domain rationale and what existing observable evidence could contradict them.

Use the same-input ordinary Bayesian baseline under each identical model. Algebraic equality with correct Bayes is expected; source/nuisance pairing, shared random numbers, marginalization and do(s) notation are not standalone innovations.

Preserve the executed swapped-nuisance and proportional-source-strength impossibility cases, and complete nuisance identity across time. A common-nuisance contrast is not a proof about marginal observed laws.

A known zero initial sensor state does not mean a zero initial environmental plume. No-flux continuous positive injection has no finite-mass steady state; arbitrary warm-up does not establish the missing ventilation or plume-age contract.

The first zero wind message is an initialization placeholder. A GMRF service reception time does not supply the age of its inputs. Pointwise wind covariance is not a calibrated joint space-time wind process; repeated unstamped observations in the current GMRF path do not justify independent nuisance samples.

Align gas/wind/pose by simulation timestamp and causal availability; count paused duplicate messages once and reject conflicts, regressions and missing required history. These are correctness prerequisites, not a new scientific contribution.

Adaptive sampling alone does not invalidate a correctly specified sequential likelihood conditioned on the observed past: for a known source-independent controller conditional on that past, policy factors cancel in source likelihood ratios. Do not invent inverse-propensity corrections or treat observed local wind as globally unbiased without establishing the relevant observation law and overlap.

Do not assume transport error is orthogonal to source sensitivity, low rank, independent of source, or bounded at a chosen scale merely to make identification succeed. Such restrictions require physical justification and an independently testable implication; gas fit alone is insufficient.
